facts.statement: The genus Sarcosuchus includes the type species Sarcosuchus imperator.
facts.quote: taxon: Sarcosuchus

facts.statement: The species Sarcosuchus hartti was originally described by Marsh in 1869.
facts.quote: subdivision: *S. hartti Marsh, 1869

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Hauterivian to Albian ages, in North Africa and Brazil.
facts.quote: Sarcosuchus (), from Ancient Greek σάρξ (sárx), meaning "flesh", and Σοῦχος (Soûkhos), meaning "Sobek", is a genus of crocodyliform that lived during the Early Cretaceous (Hauterivian to Albian ages, ) in North Africa and Brazil.

facts.statement: The genus Sarcosuchus was first described in 1966 by Frances de Broin and Philippe Taquet based on an incomplete skull found in Gadoufaoua, northern Niger.
facts.quote: The genus was first described in 1966 by French paleontologists Frances de Broin and Philippe Taquet on the basis of an incomplete skull that was discovered in Gadoufaoua, northern Niger.

facts.statement: In 1977, the species formerly known as Crocodylus hartti was reassigned to the genus Sarcosuchus.
facts.quote: In 1977, the species Crocodylus hartti, which had been discovered in Early Cretaceous deposits in Brazil in the 1850s-60s, was reassigned to Sarcosuchus.

facts.statement: Fully grown S. imperator individuals are estimated to have reached lengths of 9 to 9.5 meters and weights of 3.45 to 4.3 metric tons.
facts.quote: S. imperator is one of the biggest crocodylomorphs known, with fully grown individuals estimated to have reached up to 9 to 9.5 m in total length and 3.45 to 4.3 MT in weight.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus had telescoped eyes and a snout that accounted for 75% of the skull's length.
facts.quote: It had somewhat telescoped eyes and a long snout accounting for 75% of the length of the skull.

facts.statement: The longest reported Sarcosuchus skull is 1.7 meters long, while the longest confirmed skull is 1.6 meters long.
facts.quote: The longest reported skull is 1.7 m in length, while the longest confirmed skull is slightly shorter at 1.6 m long.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus had 35 teeth on each side of the upper jaw and 31 teeth on each side of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: There were 35 teeth in each side of the upper jaw, while in the lower jaw there were 31 teeth in each side.

facts.statement: Isotopic analyses suggest that S. imperator had a diet consisting of both fish and large dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Isotopic analyses of S. imperator bones suggest that it had a diet composed of both fish and large dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Fossils of Sarcosuchus were first discovered in the 1850s in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, by Samuel Allport.
facts.quote: Fossils of Sarcosuchus were first discovered in the Fort Montserrate and Plataforma localities in the city of Salvador, Bahia State in northeastern Brazil in the 1850s by British petrologist Samuel Allport.

facts.statement: In 1964, a French Atomic Energy Commission team discovered a nearly complete crocodylomorph skull at Gadoufaoua, Niger, while searching for uranium.
facts.quote: In 1964, a research team from the French Atomic Energy Commission looking for uranium discovered a nearly complete skull of a large crocodylomorph at the Gadoufaoua locality, a series of strata from the Elrhaz Formation in the western Ténéré of Niger.

facts.statement: In 1966, Frances de Broin and Philippe Taquet named the new species Sarcosuchus imperator based on remains from French expeditions.
facts.quote: In 1966, French paleontologists Frances de Broin and Philippe Taquet described all of the remains recovered on French expeditions as belonging to a new genus and species of pholidosaurid crocodylomorph, named Sarcosuchus imperator.

facts.statement: In 1977, Philippe Taquet and Eric Buffetaut reassigned Goniopholis hartti to Sarcosuchus based on similarities in teeth, jaws, and osteoderms.
facts.quote: In 1977, French paleontologists Philippe Taquet and Eric Buffetaut reassigned Goniopholis hartti to Sarcosuchus based on commonalities between the teeth, jaws, and osteoderms of S. imperator and G. hartti.

facts.statement: In 1997, Paul Sereno and his crew unearthed numerous Sarcosuchus remains in the Elrhaz Formation, northern Niger.
facts.quote: On his 1997 expedition to outcrops of the Elrhaz Formation in the Ténéré Desert in northern Niger, American paleontologist Paul Sereno and his crew unearthed numerous remains of dinosaurs, turtles, and Sarcosuchus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Sarcosuchus had a lifestyle similar to the Nile crocodile, hunting large terrestrial prey.
facts.quote: Sarcosuchus may have had a Nile crocodile-like lifestyle in which it hunted large, terrestrial prey.

facts.statement: Biomechanical analyses indicate that Sarcosuchus was not capable of performing a crocodile-like 'death roll'.
facts.quote: However, biomechanical analyses of Sarcosuchus fossils indicate that it was not capable of a crocodile-like "death roll".

facts.statement: The Gadoufaoua locality, where Sarcosuchus fossils were found, dates to between 125 and 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: Gadoufaoua is represented by a 175 km long-stretch of pre-Cenomanian sandstones, likely deriving from the Barremian to Albian stages of the Lower Cretaceous period. This indicates it is between 125 and 112 million years old.

facts.statement: During the Early Cretaceous, North Africa and Brazil were covered in mangrove forests and wetlands, creating a biodiversity hotspot.
facts.quote: In the Early Cretaceous, North Africa and Brazil were blanketed in mangrove forests and wetlands, fostering a hotspot of dinosaur, fish, crocodyliform, and pterosaur diversity.

facts.statement: Researchers Sereno et al. used skull length measurements to estimate the size of Sarcosuchus because a complete skeleton was unavailable.
facts.quote: This method was used by Sereno et al. (2001) for Sarcosuchus due to the absence of a complete enough skeleton.

facts.statement: The largest known skull of S. imperator measures 1.6 meters in length, leading to an estimated total body length of 11.65 meters.
facts.quote: The largest known skull of S. imperator (the type specimen) is 1.6 m long (1.5 m in the midline), and it was estimated that the individual it belonged to had a total body length of 11.65 m.

facts.statement: Some researchers argue that estimates of S. imperator size based on modern crocodilian correlations are significantly larger than reality.
facts.quote: However, extrapolation from the femur of a subadult individual as well as measurements of the skull width further showed that the largest S. imperator was significantly smaller than was estimated by Sereno et al. (2001) based on modern crocodilians.

facts.statement: O'Brien et al. (2019) estimated the largest S. imperator specimen was nearly 9 meters long and weighed 3.45 metric tons.
facts.quote: O'Brien et al. (2019) estimated the length of the largest S. imperator specimen at nearly 9 m and body mass at 3.45 MT based on longirostrine crocodylian skull width to total length and body width ratio.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus possessed a very long skull with a snout that made up approximately 75% of the total cranial length.
facts.quote: Sarcosuchus has a very long skull proportionally with a relatively elongated snout, which makes up about 75% of the total cranial length.

facts.statement: While a 1.7-meter skull has been reported, the longest confirmed skull is 1.6 meters long with a snout measuring 115 cm in length and 270 mm in width.
facts.quote: The longest reported skull is 1.7 m in length, however it remains undescribed, while the longest confirmed skull is slightly shorter at 1.6 m long, with a 115 cm long and 270 mm wide snout.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus had a snout expansion called a bulla, which is similar to the ghara found in gharials.
facts.quote: Sarcosuchus has an expansion at the end of its snout known as a bulla, which has been compared with the ghara seen in gharials.

facts.statement: The bulla in Sarcosuchus was likely not a sexually dimorphic trait because it appears in all described skulls.
facts.quote: Unlike the ghara, which is only observed in male gharials, the bulla is present in all Sarcosuchus skulls that have been described so far, suggesting that it was not a sexually dimorphic trait.

facts.statement: S. hartti teeth have false ziphodont edges with sharp, serrated patterns and smooth crenulations, unlike those of S. imperator.
facts.quote: Unlike in S. imperator, S. hartti teeth bear false ziphodont (laterally compressed (flattened), sharp, and serrated) edges, a unique pattern of lines on its enamel surface, and smooth crenulations on its carinae.

facts.statement: The jaws of S. hartti are heterodont, featuring tall anterior caniniform teeth and circular, blunt posterior teeth.
facts.quote: Furthermore, the jaws of S. hartti are heterodont, consisting of tall, enlarged anterior caniniforms and circular, blunt posterior teeth.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus is characterized by large fan-shaped expansions at the end of the lower jaw and a symphysis extending to around the 20th dentary tooth.
facts.quote: Two other diagnostic traits of the presence of large, fan-shaped expansions at the distal end of the mandibulae and a symphysis that extends posteriorly to around dentary tooth 20, two traits characteristic of Sarcosuchus.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus vertebrae are amphicoelus, a feature not found in modern crocodilians or Atoposauridae.
facts.quote: As for the postcrania, the vertebrae are amphicoelus (concave on anterior and posterior ends), a characteristic not found in crocodilians or clades like Atoposauridae.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus osteoderms on the neck and back had low keels and hook-shaped extensions, while tail osteoderms lacked these features.
facts.quote: Osteoderms are preserved in several Sarcosuchus specimens, with the cervical and dorsal osteroderms bearing low, laterally-positioned keels and hook-shaped anterolateral bony extensions.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus osteoderms formed a continuous armor from the neck to the middle of the tail, unlike gaps seen in modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Similar to Araripesuchus, the osteoderms formed a continuous cover that ran from the anterior cervical vertebrae to the middle of the caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus is classified within the clade Pholidosauridae, which is related to but distinct from the group containing modern crocodiles and alligators.
facts.quote: Sarcosuchus is commonly classified as part of the clade Pholidosauridae, a group of crocodile-like reptiles (Crocodyliformes) related but outside Crocodylia (the clade containing living crocodiles, alligators and gharials).

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus is most closely related to the North American genus Terminonaris.
facts.quote: Within this group it is most closely related to the North American genus Terminonaris.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus is considered a generalist predator, unlike most other pholidosaurids which were specialized fish eaters.
facts.quote: Sarcosuchus stands out among pholidosaurids for being considered a generalist predator, different from most known members of the clade which were specialized piscivores.

facts.statement: A 2019 study placed Sarcosuchus phylogenetically closer to Dyrosauridae within the group Tethysuchia.
facts.quote: A 2019 study found it to be in a more derived position in Tethysuchia, being phylogenetically closer to Dyrosauridae.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesized that Sarcosuchus imperator had a generalized diet including large terrestrial prey like dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Sereno et al. hypothesized that S. imperator had a generalized diet similar to that of the Nile crocodile, which would have included large terrestrial prey such as the abundant dinosaurs that lived in the same region.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus is classified in the family Pholidosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Pholidosauridae

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus was first discovered in 1947 by French paleontologist Félix de Lapparent, who found conical teeth, vertebrae, and foot scales.
facts.quote: Sarcosuchus fue descubierto por primera vez en 1947 por el paleontólogo francés Félix de Lapparent, quien encontró algunos de sus dientes cónicos, sus vértebras y las escamas de un pie.

facts.statement: Philippe Taquet named the creature Sarcosuchus imperator in 1966.
facts.quote: En 1966, Philippe Taquet llamó a esta criatura Sarcosuchus imperator.

facts.statement: Other fossils of this genus found in South America were classified as S. hartti.
facts.quote: También se descubrieron otros fósiles de este género en Brasil, América del Sur, siendo clasificados como S. hartti.

facts.statement: A 2000 expedition to the Sahara Desert found new remains of this species.
facts.quote: En 2000 se realizó una expedición al desierto del Sahara, donde se encontraron nuevos restos de esta especie.

facts.statement: Unlike other crocodiles, the skull of Sarcosuchus widens toward the front.
facts.quote: A diferencia de los cráneos de otros cocodrilos, el de Sarcosuchus se ensancha hacia la parte delantera.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus measured nearly 12 meters in length, had scales up to 30 cm long, weighed around 8,000 kg, and had a mandible measuring 1.80 meters long.
facts.quote: Medía cerca de 12 metros de largo, tenía escamas de 30 cm de largo, pesaba alrededor de 8.000 kilos y su mandíbula medía 1,80 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The morphology of Sarcosuchus was similar to that of modern gharials.
facts.quote: Su morfología era similar a la de los gaviales actuales.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus fed on fish and small to medium-sized dinosaurs caught in waterways.
facts.quote: Se alimentaba de peces y pequeños y medianos dinosaurios que atrapaba en los cursos del agua.

facts.statement: Scientists estimate Sarcosuchus reached adult size at the age of 50 to 60 years based on scale studies.
facts.quote: Los científicos estiman que el cocodrilo llegaba a su tamaño adulto a la edad de 50 o 60 años, por el estudio de sus escamas.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus coexisted with theropod dinosaurs and other crocodiles, living near river banks.
facts.quote: El Sarcosuchus coexistió con dinosaurios terópodos y otros cocodrilos, habitando cerca de la orilla de los ríos.

facts.statement: Sarcosuchus coexisted with large sauropods such as Paralititan.
facts.quote: El Sarcosuchus también coexistió con saurópodos de gran tamaño como el Paralititan.

facts.statement: The time range for the genus Sarcosuchus is from the Valanginian to the Cenomanian (137.05 to 93.9 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Cenomanian (137.05 to 93.9 million years ago)
